title: Agents' Room: Narrative Generation through Multi-step Collaboration (Huot et al., ICLR 2025)
finding: Orchestrator + planning agents (conflict, character, setting, plot) + per-section writing agents over a shared scratchpad. Expert raters preferred AR write / AR plan+write over end-to-end baselines; plan-only variants did not do well (blamed on the single finalizer). But the multi-agent stories are ~3x longer and markedly MORE repetitive than both single-call baselines and humans.
numbers: Table 2: trigram repetition intra/inter: Human 15.5/19.2; E2E zero-shot 28.8/33.4; AR-ZS plan+write 44.7/43.3; AR-FT plan+write 46.3/41.6. Unique words %: Human 50.4, E2E 44.6, AR plan+write 34-35. Length: Human 1439 words, E2E 1207, AR write ~3000-3300. 9,900 pairwise human ratings, Fleiss kappa 0.46; LLM judge vs human Spearman 0.62 by system. Win rates only in a figure I could not read.
setup: Gemini 1.5 Flash for all agents and baselines; some variants LoRA fine-tuned on Gemini Ultra synthetic data; 'Tell Me A Story' prompts.
caveats: Length is a confound the paper does not discuss: AR stories are 2.5x the baseline length and preference may track it. Per-system human preference numbers only in Figure 3, not read. No cost figures. Diversity got worse, not better, with the team.

title: HoLLMwood: Unleashing the Creativity of LLMs in Screenwriting via Role Playing (Chen et al., EMNLP Findings 2024)
finding: Writer + Editor (feedback-revision rounds) + Actor agents that role-play characters to develop plot. Beats Plan-then-Write and DOC-screen baselines; Editor feedback rounds on characters/outline win strongly over no-feedback; actor role-play is the biggest driver of 'interestingness'.
numbers: GPT-4 backbone overall win rate vs Plan-then-Write 83.0%, vs DOC-screen 79.2% (~206 pairs); GPT-3.5: 57.8% / 56.8%. Editor: outline R1 vs R0 overall 93.3%, R2 vs R0 95.0%. Role-play vs none (GPT-4) overall 75.1 vs 24.1.
setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-16k and gpt-4-0613 at temperature 1; 60 synthetic storylines over 6 genres incl. horror; screenplays compared in ~1,500-word segments.
caveats: No human evaluation at all; GPT-4 judges GPT-4 output. Baselines are other pipelines, not a single strong model plus a critique pass. No diversity or cost measure. Gains grow with backbone strength (GPT-3.5 gains are small).

title: LLM Review: Enhancing Creative Writing via Blind Peer Review Feedback
finding: Agents draft independently, critique each other's first drafts, then revise using only their own draft plus the critiques received (never peers' revisions). Beats single agent, teacher-feedback, debate and open discussion on judge scores and on novelty metrics. Authors argue seeing peers' evolving drafts aligns phrasing and themes.
numbers: SciFi-100, Llama-3.2-3B writer, GPT-4o judge 0-5: Single 3.62/3.62/3.41/3.63/3.40 (concepts/logic/characters/world/ethics); Debate 3.76/3.76/3.74/3.65/3.80; Discussion 3.94/3.89/3.90/3.74/3.73; LLM Review 3.98/4.00/3.96/4.04/4.00. Novelty 1-cos: 0.345 single, 0.424 debate, 0.435 discussion, 0.441 review. Judge-human ICC 0.58-0.65 (9 student annotators).
setup: Small writers (Llama-3.2 1B/3B, Qwen2.5 1.5B/3B) plus GPT-4o; science-fiction prompts.
caveats: Effects are ~0.3-0.4 on a 5-point judge scale with tiny models; humans only rated the winning system's output, not a comparison. Novelty measured against a reference corpus, not cross-output sameness. Discussion/debate still beat single agent on novelty, so 'interaction homogenises' is argued, not shown here.

title: Creative Generation via Multi-Agent Debate: Does Debate Suppress Diversity? (EMNLP 2026)
finding: Plain multi-agent debate raises judged quality over a single call but LOWERS diversity across independent runs, below the single-agent baseline, on every benchmark and both models. Giving each agent a persistent fixed 'lens' and restricting each agent's context to its most semantically distant peers restores and exceeds single-agent diversity at the same quality.
numbers: Qwen3-8B rubric quality Direct 66.5/73.7/64.2/74.9 vs Homo-MAD 74.0/80.6/76.3/80.2 vs Creative-MAD 71.5/82.8/76.4/80.4. Lexical diversity Div-BLEU LiveIdea: Direct 68.96, Homo-MAD 66.62, Creative-MAD 83.20; semantic Vendi 2.54/2.47/3.04. Gemma-3-12B similar (Vendi 2.69/2.44/3.51). Human pilot: Creative-MAD output set judged more diverse in 35/40 queries, quality roughly tied.
setup: Qwen3-8B and Gemma-3-12B; LiveIdeaBench, argumentative essays, MacGyver, Arena Hard v2; judge Qwen3.5-397B.
caveats: Not fiction: ideation, essays, problem solving. Small open models. Some diversity drops within std devs. Quality judged by LLM; human study is a 40-query pilot.

title: DOC: Improving Long Story Coherence With Detailed Outline Control (Yang et al., ACL 2023)
finding: A pipeline (not role agents): a detailed hierarchical outline plus a controller that keeps drafting faithful to it beats Re3 on human-judged coherence, outline relevance and interestingness. Ablation: interestingness gain comes mainly from the more detailed outline; the controller helps faithfulness and may slightly reduce interestingness.
numbers: Pairwise human, 20 stories, ~3,800 words, 1,000-1,500-word passages, 3 annotators each (Surge AI): coherent 67.6% vs 45.1%; relevant 65.3% vs 37.1%; interesting 60.1% vs 39.4%. Leaf-event faithfulness 58.5% with controller vs 37.8% without.
setup: OPT-175B drafting, text-davinci-002 for outline; 2022-era models.
caveats: Old models; small n (20 stories). Shows that explicit, detailed planning artifacts buy coherence; says nothing about role teams.

title: Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI co-creativity (Wan & Kalman; CHB: Artificial Humans 2026)
finding: Ten structurally different personas generated 300 plot ideas; ideas WITHIN a persona were near-identical, ACROSS personas very different. Feeding writers plots from the diverse pool kept collective story diversity at the human-only level, removing the convergence Doshi & Hauser (2024) saw with a single default model.
numbers: Mean cosine similarity within persona 0.92, across personas 0.20 (abstract).
setup: Persona traits: cultural background, thinking style, genre preference. Human writers, modified Doshi & Hauser design; N not in abstract.
caveats: Abstract only. Each persona alone is extremely repetitive (0.92): diversity comes from rotating many distinct seeds, consistent with ashfall's 'variety from code' rule and with prior finding that a persona prompt does not fix sameness.

title: We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs (Wenger & Kenett)
finding: Responses across 22 LLMs are far more alike than responses across humans; a population of mixed-family models is no more varied than five Llama models. 'Be very creative' prompting raises variability only modestly.
numbers: Population variability (mean cosine distance): AUT LLM 0.459 vs human 0.738 (d=2.2); FF 0.534 vs 0.835; DAT 0.665 vs 0.819. Five Llamas 0.441 vs mixed families 0.445 (p=0.41). AUT 'very creative' prompt raises variability 0.459 -> 0.576.
setup: Standard divergent-thinking tests, 7 families for stats, 102 humans.
caveats: Divergent-thinking tests, not fiction. Main implication for a team: model diversity across vendors does not buy output diversity.

title: Finding Flawed Fictions: Plot Hole Detection (Ahuja et al., 2025)
finding: LLMs detecting a planted continuity error in a story are near human on short stories but fall toward chance on long ones; more reasoning tokens mostly do not help. LLM rewrites introduce plot holes at 1.5-2x the rate of originals. Implication: an LLM 'continuity keeper' reading prose is a weak check, worse as the corpus grows.
numbers: Short: Claude 3.5 Sonnet acc 0.76 (human 0.76), GPT-4o CoT 0.64, chance 0.50. Long: o1 0.61, Claude 3.5 Sonnet+verifier 0.60, GPT-4o 0.56. o3-mini CEEval fell 0.52 -> 0.47 as effort rose. Plot-hole rate: summaries 0.45 vs originals 0.31; adaptations 0.27-0.53 vs 0.14.
setup: Facts from act one negated later; human-verified.
caveats: 2024-25 models; current models likely better but long-context degradation is the pattern.

title: Single-agent vs multi-agent under equal thinking-token budgets (Tran & Kiela, 2026)
finding: With reasoning tokens matched, a single agent matches or beats multi-agent systems on multi-hop reasoning; most reported MAS gains are unaccounted compute and context effects. MAS competitive when one agent's context use is degraded.
caveats: Abstract only; reasoning, not writing. No compute-matched study of creative writing was found (searched); every creative multi-agent paper above compares against an unmatched single call.

title: Lucasfilm Holocron and Story Group (secondary: fan wiki, press)
finding: Lucasfilm keeps canon in a FileMaker database (Holocron) of 55,000+ entries keyed by character, location, species, vehicle, run by a dedicated keeper (Leland Chee) since 2000; the Story Group (2013) is a small group that owns one canon and reviews all media. Earlier tiered canon (G/C/N levels) resolved contradictions by precedence.
caveats: Secondary sources only. Bungie's 'Destiny Historian' job ad and TV script coordinators (keep a living continuity bible, proof every script against it, report to showrunner) describe the same shape: one owner, a keyed fact store, every script checked against it.
